The core is exercised by pytest integration tests that run against a real, running stack rather than against mocks alone. Because those tests have side effects on the database, the single most important rule is to start from a clean state. Org-wide rules (branch naming, commit style, the shared CI library) are not repeated here — see Community & Standards in the Contribute to Project book.

How the core is tested

From the compose repo's README.rst "Integration tests" section:

  • pytest handles the integration tests; their requirements live in tests/requirements.txt.
  • The tests have side effects and expect a clean database. Always tear the composition's volumes down first, then bring it back up, then run the tests.

The practical sequence on the legacy stack is therefore:

# reset persistent volumes, then bring the stack back up
rmlocal down -v
rmlocal build --pull
rmlocal up
# ... wait for the stack to be healthy, then run pytest against it

Not yet documented. The exact command for running the integration pytest suite against a running stack — on the host from tests/requirements.txt, or inside the rmapi container — is still to be written here.

Skipping the down -v reset is the most common cause of flaky or false test failures, because leftover users, invite codes, and certificates from a previous run pollute the assertions. See Iterate on the core API (Docker Compose) for the full down/up dance and how to switch between rmlocal and rmdev safely.

Product integration tests (for contract awareness)

Product integration APIs ship their own pytest suites that assert the callback contract from the other side. The Copier scaffold (pvarki/python-integration-template) and the Matrix reference (pvarki/python-matrix-rmapi) both generate tests under tests/ (for example test_crud.py, test_openapi.py) and run them via uv / nox / tox and Docker devel_shell / tox targets. When you change the core's callback behaviour, expect those downstream suites to be the early-warning system — keep the contract documented on Core APIs & the rmapi contract stable.

pre-commit

The compose repo's README.rst "pre-commit notes" section: run pre-commit run --all-files liberally, and make sure you have installed the hooks first:

pre-commit install --install-hooks
pre-commit run --all-files
If pre-commit complains about missing environment variables, source the example env first:
source example_env.sh

What gates a merge

  • CI runs on every push/PR (build + checks). The build badge at the top of the compose README.rst reflects the aggregate build workflow.
  • pre-commit / lint must pass.
  • Integration tests must pass against a clean database.

The concrete CI configuration is shared across pvarki repos through pvarki/config-ci-library, and markdown/docs conventions through pvarki/markdown-pvarki-best_practises. Both are documented and linked from Community & Standards in Contribute to Project — defer to that page for the authoritative org rules rather than duplicating them here.
